newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Senate won't finish Telstra Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Senate won't finish Telstra Tuesday.

text.p: The Australian Senate will not complete debate on the Telstra Corp privatisation bill on Tuesday, a government spokesman said.
"It should be tomorrow," the spokesman for government Senate leader Robert Hill told Reuters.

Completion of the Telstra bill has repeatedly fallen behind schedule over the past week. It was supposed to be voted on finally on Monday, but the minority parties launched extended debate on proposed amendments.
The Senate does not spend all of its time debating government business, such as this bill.
At 0320 GMT (2.20 p.m.) the Senate was in question time and was expected to conduct government business for only an hour after that before going on to other matters for the remainder of Tuesday.
The bill is the Senate's amendment mode, called the committee of the whole, and shortly before 0300 GMT rejected a batch of amendments by the Democrats minority party.
But many more amendments are expected, including the current one proposed by key independent Brian Harradine.

Harradine's motion, to delay the bill's commencement by a few months, is his joint amendment with the government, embodying part of the agreement under which he is expected to finally vote for the bill.

Harradine and the other independent, Mal Colston, have expressed concerns about voting for the bill over the past few months but the government answered those concerns with spending packages last week.
So their final support for the bill is expected.
The bill, the Telstra (Dilution of Public Ownership) Bill, would authorise the sale of a third of Telstra's equity, which the government says is worth about A$8 billion.
This is scheduled to be the last week of parliamentary sittings for the year.

Contentious budget bills, in which about a quarter of the government's fiscal tightening is at risk, are supposed to follow the Telstra bill in the Senate and be completed by Friday, together with some non-contentious bills.
